boundary_rationale: The row opens on a fresh title-stack formula paired with a plural imperative, oshb:Jer.9.16 = web:Jer.9.17, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֛וּ וְקִרְא֥וּ לַמְקוֹנְנ֖וֹת (oshb:Jer.9.16, byte tier) — ‘koh amar YHWH tsevaot, hitbonenu veqir'u lamqonenot,’ ‘thus says Yahweh of Armies, consider, and call for the mourning women’ — summoning professional mourners rather than announcing judgment directly. The summons turns to address the women themselves, oshb:Jer.9.19 = web:Jer.9.20, כִּֽי שְׁמַ֤עְנָה נָשִׁים֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.9.19, byte tier) — ‘ki shema'nah nashim devar YHWH,’ ‘yet hear Yahweh's word, you women’ — instructing them to teach the lament, and closes on the content that lament answers, oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22, דַּבֵּ֗ר כֹּ֚ה נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה וְנָֽפְלָה֙ נִבְלַ֣ת הָֽאָדָ֔ם כְּדֹ֖מֶן עַל פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה (oshb:Jer.9.21, byte tier) — ‘dabber koh ne'um YHWH, venafelah nivlat ha-adam kedomen al-penei hasadeh,’ ‘speak, thus is the declaration of Yahweh, the dead bodies of men will fall as dung on the surface of the field’ — a singular imperative that names what the mourning is for rather than opening an unrelated address. The row closes there because web:Jer.9.23 = oshb:Jer.9.22 turns to an unrelated wisdom saying with its own fresh koh-amar onset.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The 'speak' command at web:Jer.9.22 = oshb:Jer.9.21 could open its own short row, since it addresses a singular hearer rather than the women addressed from web:Jer.9.20 = oshb:Jer.9.19 onward, but its dung-and-harvest image continues the death already named in the same verse rather than introducing an unrelated topic, so it is kept as the summons unit's closing image.

A petuchah closes oshb:Jer.9.15, immediately before the row, a setumah falls inside it at oshb:Jer.9.18, and another closes it at oshb:Jer.9.21 (single-witness, WLC).

boundary_rationale: The row opens on the recurring judgment formula, oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25, הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.9.24, byte tier) — ‘hineh yamim ba'im, ne'um YHWH,’ ‘behold, the days come, says Yahweh’ — verse-initial here, unlike the same consonantal formula's therefore-prefixed, non-verse-initial appearance opening the Topheth threat earlier in the book, לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ (oshb:Jer.7.32 = web:Jer.7.32, byte tier), one of 15 verses book-wide carrying the run (sweep: 15 verses, skeleton tier), now opening a circumcision oracle. The nation roster, oshb:Jer.9.25 = web:Jer.9.26, עַל מִצְרַ֣יִם וְעַל יְהוּדָ֗ה וְעַל אֱד֞וֹם (oshb:Jer.9.25, byte tier) — naming Egypt, Judah, and Edom beside “all who have the corners of their hair cut off, who dwell in the wilderness” (web:Jer.9.26), closes on the verdict, כִּ֤י כָל הַגּוֹיִם֙ עֲרֵלִ֔ים וְכָל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַרְלֵי לֵֽב (oshb:Jer.9.25, byte tier) — ‘ki khol ha-goyim arelim ve-khol beit Yisrael arlei lev,’ ‘for all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.’
strongest_rejected_alternative: The nation roster and its verdict (9.26) could be split into two short rows at the list-to-verdict turn, but the roster serves the verdict that closes the same sentence rather than standing as independent content, so they are kept as one unit.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a plural summons, שִׁמְע֣וּ אֶת הַדָּבָ֗ר (oshb:Jer.10.1, byte), matching “Hear the word which Yahweh speaks to you, house of Israel!” (web:Jer.10.1). A koh-amar onset follows at once, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.10.2, byte), placing the opening idol mockery in Yahweh's own mouth. The speech does not hold a single mouth for its whole length: a second-person address praising Yahweh directly breaks in, מֵאֵ֥ין כָּמ֖וֹךָ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה (oshb:Jer.10.6, byte) — “There is no one like you, Yahweh. You are great,” (web:Jer.10.6) — continued at מִ֣י לֹ֤א יִֽרָאֲךָ֙ (oshb:Jer.10.7, byte); a third-person predication about Yahweh follows at וַֽיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ אֱמֶ֔ת (oshb:Jer.10.10, byte); and the address returns to the plural nations addressees at the Aramaic close. No fresh koh-amar onset, addressee-naming imperative, or discourse frame opens a rival unit at any of these turns, so the alternation of mockery, praise addressed to Yahweh, and predication about Yahweh is read as one continuous speech rather than divided at these internal turns. It closes on an Aramaic sentence, כִּדְנָה֙ תֵּאמְר֣וּן לְה֔וֹם אֱלָ֣הַיָּ֔א דִּֽי שְׁמַיָּ֥א וְאַרְקָ֖א לָ֣א עֲבַ֑דוּ (oshb:Jer.10.11, byte) — “You shall say this to them: ‘The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth, and from under the heavens.’” (web:Jer.10.11) — a self-contained Aramaic island inside the surrounding Hebrew, functioning as the refutation formula Israel is told to hand back to the nations; the opening verb is a prefix-conjugation form with the paragogic nun, rendered as a modal future rather than an imperative, and it belongs with the preceding mockery. The row is cut here because verse 12 opens a distinct hymnic unit in Hebrew rather than continuing this address.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the second-person praise addressed to Yahweh, or the third-person predication about Yahweh, out of the surrounding idol mockery into separate rows was rejected because no koh-amar onset, addressee-naming imperative, or discourse frame marks a fresh seam at any of these turns; the mockery, the praise, and the predication interleave inside the same continuous speech.
literature_type_guess: idol polemic with interleaved praise and an embedded refutation formula

Verse 11's Aramaic is a structural feature of this stretch of text, not a footnote to it: oshb:Jer.10.11 = web:Jer.10.11 is the book's single Aramaic-coded verse, a self-contained island inside the surrounding Hebrew idol polemic. boundary_rationale: The address turns from third-person report of the rumor out of the north, ק֤וֹל שְׁמוּעָה֙ הִנֵּ֣ה בָאָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.10.22, byte) — “The voice of news, behold, it comes,” (web:Jer.10.22) — into first-person petition addressed to Yahweh, יָדַ֣עְתִּי יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י לֹ֥א לָאָדָ֖ם דַּרְכּ֑וֹ (oshb:Jer.10.23, byte), matching “Yahweh, I know that the way of man is not in himself.” (web:Jer.10.23). The prayer moves from submission to correction into an imprecation against the nations that devoured Jacob, שְׁפֹ֣ךְ חֲמָתְךָ֗ עַל הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא יְדָע֔וּךָ (oshb:Jer.10.25, byte), matching “Pour out your wrath on the nations that don't know you,” (web:Jer.10.25), without a new formula or addressee change between the two movements, so both stand as one unit. The unit, and the surrounding narrative frame that opened at Jer.7.1, close together at this verse.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the submission plea in verses 23-24 from the imprecation in verse 25 into separate rows was rejected because both remain addressed to Yahweh in the same first-person prayer voice across the turn from petition to imprecation.
literature_type_guess: communal prayer of submission and imprecation

boundary_rationale: A prose-sermon superscription opens the unit, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.11.1, byte), matching “The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.11.1) — byte-identical across the whole verse to the header that opened the temple sermon at oshb:Jer.7.1, and sharing its header-core construction with 11 verses book-wide (sweep: 11 verses, skeleton tier), here introducing a covenant sermon instead. The commission continues without a break through the summons to hear, “Hear the words of this covenant,” (web:Jer.11.2), and the covenant-curse content it introduces, closing on Jeremiah's own reply to what he has been told to say, וָאַ֥עַן וָאֹמַ֖ר אָמֵ֥ן יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.11.5, byte) — “Amen, Yahweh.” (web:Jer.11.5). The row is cut there because a fresh introduction, Yahweh said to me, reopens address at verse 6 with a new command to proclaim, after Jeremiah's reply has closed this initial exchange.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through the historical recap that follows was rejected because a fresh Yahweh-said-to-me introduction reopens address at verse 6, after Jeremiah's own reply closes the initial commissioning exchange.

boundary_rationale: The same narrative-introduction formula reopens address, וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י נִֽמְצָא קֶ֨שֶׁר֙ (oshb:Jer.11.9, byte) — “Yahweh said to me,” (web:Jer.11.9) — with a change of grammatical subject: a conspiracy among the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, who are then said to have returned to their forefathers' iniquities. boundary_rationale: A discourse-frame prohibition opens the unit, וְאַתָּ֗ה אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ בְּעַד הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.11.14, byte), matching “Therefore don't pray for this people.” (web:Jer.11.14), addressed to the prophet himself. The verses that follow shift the addressee again, מֶ֣ה לִֽידִידִ֞י בְּבֵיתִ֗י (oshb:Jer.11.15, byte) speaking of the beloved in Yahweh's own house, and the olive-tree image, זַ֤יִת רַֽעֲנָן֙ יְפֵ֣ה פְרִי תֹ֔אַר (oshb:Jer.11.16, byte) — “A green olive tree, beautiful with goodly fruit.” (web:Jer.11.16) — addresses a feminine figure rather than the prophet, by a second-person feminine chain running from שְׁמֵ֑ךְ closing verse 16 through וַיהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ הַנּוֹטֵ֣עַ אוֹתָ֔ךְ and עָלַ֖יִךְ in verse 17 (oshb:Jer.11.16-Jer.11.17, byte); that shift is disclosed rather than used to cut a new row, since verse 17 is bound back to verse 16 by this chain rather than by any fresh formula, the planter of verse 17, וַיהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ הַנּוֹטֵ֣עַ אוֹתָ֔ךְ (oshb:Jer.11.17, byte), naming the same feminine figure just addressed in verse 16. The row is cut before verse 18 because that verse turns to Jeremiah's own first-person account of a plot against him, a wholly different scene.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at the shift from the prophet as addressee in verse 14 to the feminine figure addressed from verse 15 onward was considered, since the referent plainly changes, but no koh-amar onset or discourse imperative accompanies the shift, and verse 17 is bound back to verse 16 by the same second-person feminine chain, not by a fresh formula, so the four verses are held as one unit rather than certain.
